description.narrative: The proposed results-based lending (RBL) program aims to significantly improve the financial sustainability and service delivery performance of 39 of Pakistan's commercial state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and National Highway Authority (NHA), the largest loss-maker in the country's SOE portfolio. These SOEs place a considerable burden on overall economic productivity and undermine the government's overarching goal of a prosperous, equitable, and thriving economy.

Output: Service performance and financial sustainability of NHA improved Indicator: At least 80% of the technical staff capacity required by NHA as per the SHRM plan (of which 10% are women) are recruited in a transparent and merit-based process (2024 baseline: No SHRM plan in place; technical staffing inadequate; no centralized mechanism for transformation and digitization) (CRF indicators 4, 7, 10, and 11) Data Source: NHA recruitment reports and SHRM Actual value:

Output: Service performance and financial sustainability of NHA improved Indicator: Climate vulnerability risk assessments of 100% of the NHA network completed and targeted risk mitigation strategies are identified and implemented on 50% of identified segments (2024 baseline: No updated climate vulnerability risk assessments of the NHA network and no follow-up mitigation measures) (CRF indicators 9, 10, 11, and 12) Data Source: NHA's assessment records, climate risk assessment, and mitigation reports Actual value:

Output: Service performance and financial sustainability of NHA improved Indicator: The iRAP Star Rating Assessments are completed for NHA networks, 90% of Star Rating Assessments are maintained and up to date, and safety upgrades are implemented in identified locationsc (2024 baseline: 10% of high-risk segments completed with planned safety upgrades) (CRF indicators 9 and 11) Data Source: NHA program records and assessment reports Actual value:

Output: Compliance with the SOEs (Governance and Operations) Act, 2023 (SOE Act) and SOEs Ownership and Management Policy, 2023 (SOE Policy) improved Indicator: (i) 39 target entities make their audited financial statements publicly available, and (ii) audited financial statements of 33 target entities are compliant with IFRS as published by the IASB (DLI 2) (2024 baseline: 15 entities publish audited financial statements and audited financial statements of 8 entities are compliant with IFRSc) (CRF indicator 11) Data Source: Finance Division reports, audited statements and auditor reports Actual value:

Output: Service performance and financial sustainability of NHA improved Indicator: (i) All debt of the NHA associated with commercially non-viable projects before the start of the RBL program is restructured, including the noncommercial portion of the prospective throw-forward amount; (ii) debt stock reduced by 100% to achieve an optimal capital structure for NHA; and (iii) all noncommercial ongoing projects are funded in accordance with Section 7(4) and Schedule II of the SOE Act (DLI 6) (2024 baseline: $4.8 billion in debt principal; $1.2 billion in associated accrued interest; about $ 6.9 billion throw-forward for ongoing projects) (CRF indicators 11 and 3) Data Source: All financial records and reports on NHA's CDLs and on current and ongoing PSOs Actual value:

Output: Service performance and financial sustainability of NHA improved Indicator: 95% of all NHA assets, including roads, bridges, and infrastructure facilities, digitized and mapped via GISs and 30% of digitized roadside commercial amenities are integrated into NHA's revenue stream (2024 baseline: 50% of assets mapped via GISs and verified, 5% of commercial roadside amenities are in revenue net of NHA) (CRF indicators 10, 11, and 12) Data Source: NHA's management system for assets and commercial amenities Actual value:

Output: Service performance and financial sustainability of NHA improved Indicator: Procurement and billing of contracts are conducted via e-procurement and billing systems, with e-procurement covering 100% of development contracts and 80% of nondevelopment contracts; and e-billing covering 90% of development contracts and 80% of no-development contracts (2024 baseline: e-procurement covers 75% of development contracts and 0% of nondevelopment contracts; e-billing covers 10% of development contracts, and 0% of nondevelopment contracts.) (CRF indicator 11) Data Source: NHA's procurement and billing system records Actual value:
